subject: Behavioral Economics
title: Commitment Devices for Saving
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: Commitment Devices for Saving.

hook.text: In the Philippines, farmers locked savings in an account they couldn't access until a goal date. Savings rose 82%.

buildup.text: Commitment devices restrict future choices to help people follow through on intentions.

discovery.text: Ashraf showed that people willingly choose restricted accounts even at lower interest rates.

twist.text: Too rigid a commitment backfires. If emergencies arise and the money is locked, people lose trust in the system.

climax.text: The best commitment devices are strict enough to prevent impulse but flexible enough for genuine emergencies.

punchline.text: We save more when we lock the door and hide the key.

quiz.question: Why do people voluntarily choose restricted savings accounts?
options: They offer the highest interest rates
The constraint helps overcome present bias and impulsive spending
Banks require restricted accounts by law
